title: Negative Staining

references.label: General microbiology/molecular biology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)

purpose: To visualize bacterial cell size and shape with minimal distortion, particularly useful for cells or structures that are damaged or shrunk by heat-fixation and direct staining.
principle: An acidic dye (such as nigrosin or India ink) carries a negative charge and is repelled by the also-negatively-charged bacterial cell surface, so the dye stains the background around the cells rather than the cells themselves; the unstained cells appear as bright, translucent shapes against a uniformly dark background, avoiding the heat-fixation step (and its associated shrinkage/distortion) required by most direct staining methods.
requiredMaterials: Second slide (for the spreading technique) or coverslip
requiredReagents: Acidic stain such as nigrosin or India ink

procedure.instruction: Place a small drop of the stain near one end of a clean slide.
Mix a loopful of bacterial culture into the stain drop.
Using the edge of a second slide held at an angle, spread the mixture into a thin film across the slide (a technique similar to a blood smear), without heat-fixing.
Air-dry completely without heat before examining.
Examine under oil immersion, looking for translucent/unstained cells against the dark, stained background.

observations: Bright, translucent bacterial cells of relatively natural size and shape, standing out clearly against a uniformly dark background.
interpretation: Because no heat-fixation or harsh staining chemistry is applied directly to the cells, this method is considered to give a size and shape closer to the cell's natural, unstained appearance than heat-fixed stains, useful for accurate morphological assessment or for organisms prone to distortion by other methods.
criticalNotes: Do not heat-fix the smear — the entire value of this method depends on avoiding the shrinkage/distortion that heat-fixation can cause.
precautions: Follow standard aseptic technique when preparing the smear from a live culture.
Handle stain reagents per their safety data sheets.
biosafetyNotes: Handle the source culture per its specific biosafety risk assessment.
limitations: Provides morphological information only (size, shape, arrangement) and does not differentiate Gram reaction or other structural/staining-based characteristics.
A film spread too thick can obscure individual cells against the dense background stain.
